decisions.reason: Material change: the 2026-10-29 doc gives a 90-day default expiry, with owner-set 7-180 days for repository facts. The prior review recorded 28 days. This fetch states no stage for Copilot Memory; only Copilot Dreaming is called public preview. Lifecycle is unverified. No tenant evidence was fetched, so every gate stays unknown. Human dates are not renewed.

citations.quote: The default expiry period is 90 days. Enterprise and organization owners can configure the expiry period for repository-level facts to any value between 7 and 180 days (inclusive).
Copilot Memory is available on all paid Copilot plans.
Memories are only created when the applicable settings allow that type of memory.
Copilot Dreaming is in public preview and is subject to change.

findings.reason: Doc says all paid plans and lists surfaces. It states no release stage for Memory itself; only Dreaming is public preview. No pilot-cohort test.
findings.next: Confirm Memory stage in an official source; test a permitted and an ineligible identity.

findings.reason: Doc says plan settings and policies decide use, and owners set repository-fact expiry. No negative enforcement test was fetched.
findings.next: Disable Memory for a test identity and verify local settings cannot override it.

findings.reason: User-level preferences follow a user across repositories; repository facts are shared with collaborators. Scope and credential evidence is absent.

findings.reason: Expiry is 90 days by default (7-180 for repository facts); user preferences stay at the default. Hidden memories can remain stored until expiry. Residency and deletion evidence is absent.
findings.next: Review the data flow with synthetic data; prove deletion of repository and user memories.
